title: Website Returns HTTP 403 Forbidden or 404 Not Found
symptom: End users accessing a web application receive HTTP 403 Forbidden or HTTP 404 Not Found response.
initial_observations: Web server is running and responding.
Specific routes or static assets fail.
environment: EC2 running Nginx or Apache HTTP Server.

possible_causes.cause: Web server worker user lacks read/execute permissions on document root files
possible_causes.evidence_needed: Nginx error.log: 'directory index of /var/www/html is forbidden' or '13: Permission denied'.
possible_causes.remediation: Fix ownership and permissions: `chown -R nginx:nginx /var/www/html` and `chmod -R 755 /var/www/html`.

possible_causes.cause: Missing index file (index.html or index.php) with directory autoindex disabled
possible_causes.evidence_needed: Directory exists but contains no recognized index file.
possible_causes.remediation: Create required index.html or configure directory listing if intentional.

investigation_steps.title: Check Web Server Error Log
investigation_steps.explanation: Web server logs state exact reason for 403 or 404.
investigation_steps.what_to_look_for: Look for 'Permission denied' or 'No such file or directory'.

investigation_steps.title: Verify File Permissions on Document Root
investigation_steps.explanation: Verify read and execute bits on path leading to content.
investigation_steps.what_to_look_for: Owner matching web server user and +r +x permissions.

prevention: Include correct file permission enforcement in CI/CD deployment scripts.
